question: How should stored data be migrated when a Soroban contract upgrade changes its data structures?

golden.answer: A Wasm update, which the contract must gate with its own authorization check, keeps the contract's address and storage but converts nothing: keys and value layouts must stay compatible or be migrated, or old data is stranded. As of 2026-11-14, contracts built with soroban-sdk v28+ (CAP-86) read named-field structs sparsely: an added `Option` field reads as `None` and a removed field is ignored; other changes still need migration. Version stored records; migrate lazily or through an idempotent entrypoint over bounded batches. Test on production-shaped state.
keyFacts: An upgrade converts no stored data; keys and layouts must stay compatible or migrate.
Versioned records support lazy migration or an explicit controlled migration entrypoint.
Large migrations are idempotent and batched to fit transaction resource limits.
SDK v28+ reads an added `Option` field as `None`; other schema changes need migration.
avoid: Do NOT say uploading new Wasm re-encodes existing storage values.
Do NOT say every migration must fit in one transaction.
golden.notes: Saying a pre-v28 build traps with `UnexpectedSize` on an added field is correct; it is wrong only for an added `Option` field or removed field of a named-field struct on a v28+ build.

Versioned records can be migrated lazily or through a controlled explicit migration entrypoint.
Large migrations should be idempotent and batched to fit transaction resource limits.
Uploading new Wasm automatically re-encodes all existing storage values.
Every migration must fit into one transaction.

truth.notes: As of 2026-11-02: CAP-86 sparse unpacking applies only to contracts rebuilt with soroban-sdk v28+. Non-Option field additions, type changes, enums, and tuple structs still need migration. Recommending versioned records for every schema change remains correct. The official migrate-contract-storage guide still says reading a stored DataV1 as a DataV2 with an added Option field traps with Error(Object, UnexpectedSize), with no SDK-version scope (observed 2026-11-02; improvements/stellar-docs/sd-070-migrate-contract-storage-cap-86-scope.md). That trap claim is correct for pre-v28 builds, and a v28+ read still errors on a missing non-Option field. It is wrong only when the answer says that, on a v28+ build, an added Option field or a removed field of a named-field struct traps.
